🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO STANDS BY BACHELET FOR UN CHIEF — EVEN AFTER CHILE WALKED</u>

Mexico and Brazil are keeping Michelle Bachelet's candidacy for UN Secretary-General alive after Chile's government pulled its own sponsorship in March and she slipped in the Security Council's second straw poll. Sheinbaum called her "a woman with a lot of experience who seeks peace in the world," backing a Latin American woman for the top UN post on a platform of human rights and multilateralism — while the region's right abandons one of its own.

🇲🇽🛡️ <u>MEXICO PUTS FOREIGN CAPITAL UNDER NATIONAL-SECURITY LOCK</u>

Sheinbaum sent Congress a reform giving a beefed-up National Foreign Investment Commission — now seated with Defense, the Navy, intelligence and the treasury's financial-crimes unit — veto power over any foreign buyer seeking more than 49% of Mexican firms in energy, mining, ports, data centers, semiconductors, AI or defense. The state gets 60 days to green-light, condition, or block a deal on national-security grounds. The US has screened foreign money in its strategic sectors for decades; Mexico is now claiming the same right over its own ground.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexican forces seize an arsenal of 6,000+ explosives in Chihuahua</u>

Federal forces seized a cartel arsenal of more than 6,000 explosive devices in Chihuahua — part of coordinated operations that also struck Sinaloa, netting an encampment, 33 long guns, cocaine, marijuana and detentions. Mexican intelligence, Mexican forces: the war-grade stockpiles left by the neoliberal era, dismantled on Mexican soil. (La Jornada)

🇲🇽💰 <u>Mexico's FDI hits a record $34.97 billion</u>

Mexico drew a record $34.968 billion in foreign direct investment in the first half of 2026 — the highest first-half ever, up 2.1% year-on-year and nearly double (+89.7%) the 2021 figure. The US still leads with $16.871B (48.2% of the total), ahead of Spain and Canada: foreign capital doubling down on Mexico in five years, tariff war and all. (El Economista)

🇲🇽🏘️ <u>MC's Guadalajara: a real-estate business that expels its own</u>

Under Movimiento Ciudadano governments and mayor Verónica Delgadillo, Guadalajara has been run as a real-estate business, El Soberano reports. More than 110,000 people have been pushed to service-less peripheries in a decade, rents have climbed as much as 273%, and Airbnb speculation hollows out historic barrios — while young tapatíos earning around 17,000 pesos a month are priced out of their own city.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Sheinbaum on García Luna: the hypocrisy of his old defenders</u>

President Sheinbaum called out the "hipocresía" of those who defended Genaro García Luna and now feign distance. Under Calderón — with García Luna running security — the Mexican state "tomó partido por un grupo delictivo," she said, allying with one cartel against the rest while daily homicides jumped from 27 to over 70. That was the neoliberal drug war, armed in part by Fast and Furious. Today, she noted, a suspect means an investigation, a warrant and a court — not a state pact with crime. (Contralínea)

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Peña Nieto resurfaces — beside his Pegasus dealer</u>

Ex-president Enrique Peña Nieto reappeared at a lavish wedding in Portofino, Italy — seated beside Avishai Neriah, the Israeli businessman who says he and a partner funneled ~$25M to EPN's circle between 2012 and 2018 to lock in the Pegasus spyware contracts. That's the same Pegasus that made Mexico NSO Group's largest client and was turned on journalists, activists and rivals. The FGR has an open file on the alleged bribes. (La Jornada)

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>Rosa Icela to Morena: Mexico above party</u>

As Congress opens its new session, Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez told Morena's deputies to put the interest of the Mexican people above party or self — "nadie puede servirse del movimiento." She pressed them to back President Sheinbaum's reforms, including the constitutional change requiring the president and governors to hold Mexican nationality only, and to guard AMLO's legacy and the movement's unity.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Mexico added 671K jobs in July — but a record share were informal</u>

INEGI's July survey shows 670,991 jobs added, the year's strongest monthly gain — yet informal employment hit an all-time high of 34.14 million, 56.2% of all workers. Across January–July the economy added 1.15 million informal jobs while formal payrolls shed 776,501; unemployment held at 2.9%. Real growth, with formalization still the unfinished task. (El Economista)

🇲🇽📺 <u>Mexico restores audience rights: separate news from opinion, ads from content</u>

The telecom regulator (CRT) approved new audience-rights guidelines requiring open TV and radio to give the public truthful information, clearly separate news from opinion and advertising from content, guarantee the right of reply, and protect minors — protections gutted in the neoliberal era under media-industry pressure. Refined from 8,889 public comments and effective 30 days after publication, the rules stop short of policing content: the regulator says it won't judge which news is true or false, only that outlets honor the complaint process. (El Soberano)
